gap.reason: Stage 2 decomposition critic repair: The login floor is materially useful, but it replaces the source authentication boundary with a proxy. The requirement is that the user enters their MID and password to gain role-based entry; the schema exposes only a Credential owner and hasPassword flag, not request-entered MID/password values or a password/MID verification result. Requiring context.credential.user == principal and hasPassword does not represent successful authentication with the entered MID and password.

proposed_atoms.name: login
proposed_atoms.rationale: The login action needs request authentication evidence so policies can require the entered MID to identify the principal and the entered password to have been verified.
proposed_atoms.plain_english_summary: This adds the information supplied and checked during login so access can depend on a real successful login attempt.
proposed_atoms.source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.

enteredMid.name: login__context__enteredMid
enteredMid.rationale: The request-entered MID is needed to compare the login identifier against the principal's MID.
enteredMid.plain_english_summary: The MID typed by the user during login.

gap.reason: Stage 2 decomposition critic repair: The source grant is not merely generic access to the patient's ProviderList; it is specifically to view LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and LHCPs the patient has designated. The proposed floor correctly includes the own-patient boundary and active-session boundary, but it accepts ProviderList as a proxy even though the schema does not expose an office-visit history relationship and does not connect ProviderList to ProviderDesignation/isDesignated membership. Repair is needed to make the prior-office-visit and designated-LHCP boundaries explicit; if those cannot be represented with the current schema, this is a schema gap rather than an acceptable proxy.

proposed_atoms.name: OfficeVisit
proposed_atoms.rationale: OfficeVisit represents the historical encounter relationship needed to identify LHCPs a patient has previously visited.
proposed_atoms.plain_english_summary: A record that a patient had an office visit with a particular LHCP.
proposed_atoms.source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.

proposed_atoms.name: OfficeVisit__patient
proposed_atoms.rationale: The office visit must be tied to the patient whose prior LHCP relationship is being checked.
proposed_atoms.plain_english_summary: The patient who had the office visit.
proposed_atoms.source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.
alternatives_considered: Inferred from the phrase "the patient has ever had an office visit with"; alternatively could store only a Set<Lhcp> on ProviderList, but that would lose the visit relationship object.

proposed_atoms.name: OfficeVisit__lhcp
proposed_atoms.rationale: The office visit must identify the LHCP involved so policies can distinguish prior-visit LHCPs.
proposed_atoms.plain_english_summary: The LHCP who participated in the patient's office visit.
proposed_atoms.source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.
alternatives_considered: Inferred from the phrase "LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with"; alternatively could use a generic Hcp, but the requirement specifically names LHCPs.

proposed_atoms.name: ProviderList__officeVisits
proposed_atoms.rationale: ProviderList needs an explicit hook to the patient's office-visit history rather than acting as an undifferentiated provider proxy.
proposed_atoms.plain_english_summary: The office visits that establish which LHCPs the patient has previously seen.
proposed_atoms.source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.
alternatives_considered: Store priorOfficeVisitLhcps as Set<Lhcp> directly on ProviderList; rejected because an OfficeVisit entity preserves the patient-LHCP relationship explicitly.

proposed_atoms.name: ProviderList__designations
proposed_atoms.rationale: ProviderList needs an explicit connection to ProviderDesignation entities so policies can test patient-specific designated-LHCP membership and isDesignated state.
proposed_atoms.plain_english_summary: The provider designations that show which LHCPs the patient has designated.
proposed_atoms.source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.
alternatives_considered: Store designatedLhcps as Set<Lhcp> directly on ProviderList; rejected because existing ProviderDesignation already carries patient, LHCP, and isDesignated state.

gap.reason: Stage 2 decomposition critic repair: The add-provider safety bound is materially useful, but this proposed ceiling accepts a proxy for the source workflow. The source scopes the add operation not only to the patient's own provider list and an active session, but also to adding a provider found by search by provider name, specialty, and optionally zip code. Prior review already identified the unresolved search/name matching boundary; a ceiling that omits it would allow policies to add arbitrary providers as long as the list is owned by the patient. Because the current schema does not provide a reliable provider-name/search-match hook for Hcp/Lhcp, repair is needed rather than accepting the own-list proxy.

proposed_atoms.name: Hcp__name
proposed_atoms.rationale: The add-provider workflow needs a provider name field on Hcp so policies can compare the selected provider to the searched name.
proposed_atoms.plain_english_summary: This stores the provider's name for matching provider-list search results.
proposed_atoms.source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
alternatives_considered: Use User.name through Hcp membership; rejected because the current Cedar schema does not make inherited User attributes reliably available on Hcp entities.
Represent search matching only in action context; rejected because the selected provider still needs a provider-side name hook.

proposed_atoms.name: Hcp__specialty
proposed_atoms.rationale: The add-provider workflow needs a provider specialty field on Hcp so policies can compare the selected provider to the searched specialty.
proposed_atoms.plain_english_summary: This stores the provider's specialty for matching provider-list search results.
proposed_atoms.source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
alternatives_considered: Use only Lhcp.specialty; rejected because the action context provider is typed as Hcp and the source says LHCP/HCP.
Represent specialty only as searchSpecialty in action context; rejected because the selected provider still needs a provider-side specialty hook.

proposed_atoms.name: Hcp__zipCode
proposed_atoms.rationale: The add-provider workflow needs an optional provider zip-code field on Hcp so policies can compare the selected provider to an optional searched zip code.
proposed_atoms.plain_english_summary: This stores the provider's zip code when available for matching provider-list search results.
proposed_atoms.source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
alternatives_considered: Use only Lhcp.zipCode; rejected because the add-provider action selects a provider typed as Hcp.
Represent zip code only as searchZipCode in action context; rejected because the selected provider still needs a provider-side zip-code hook.
